title: The plainest opening range breakout on QQQ beat buy and hold over the last 4 and a half years
author: person-person12
selftext:
Everybody sells a complicated version of this one. I wanted to see what the **plainest possible version** does with nothing added to it.

The rules, and thats all of them:

* mark the high and the low of the first 15 minutes after the open
* first 5 minute candle that closes outside that range, take it in that direction
* stop goes on the other side of the range
* target is two range widths away
* one trade a day, no entries after 11:30, flat at 15:55

QQQ, 5 minute candles, **Sept 2021 to March 2026**, 100k, fully invested on each trade, commission and slippage charged on both sides. I ran it in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) and it replayed about 89,000 candles.

**What came back:**

* 1,062 trades
* 48.3% win rate
* profit factor 1.17
* **100k to $163,576, so +63.6%**
* max drawdown 10.7%

QQQ itself went from about 382 to about 568 across that same window, so **buy and hold was roughly +48%**, and it got there through a much uglier drawdown, 2022 being the obvious one.

**\_\_\_\_\_\_**

The three parts I did not expect:

**The short side made more than the long side** in a window where the index rose 48%. 521 shorts made $35,879 and 541 longs made $27,697. It is flat overnight every night, so it never wore a single gap in either direction.

**Only 22% of trades ever reached the target.** 434 got stopped out, 234 hit the 2x, and the other 394 just got closed at 15:55 wherever they happened to be sitting. That middle bucket won 70.8% of the time and made $134,327, which is more work than the target is doing.

**Costs took a quarter of it.** $84,370 gross, $20,791 of commission and slippage, $63,579 net. Three cents a share and a dollar a round trip does that over a thousand trades.

Every year was green. 2022 +$14,971, 2025 +$19,458, and the weakest was 2024 at +$6,264.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

A few things make this less impressive than it reads, and id want somebody to say them if it was my strategy on the table.

It is one instrument and one set of choices. I picked 15 minutes and a 2x target because thats the version people teach, not because I ran twenty variants and kept the flattering one. A window that contains one enormous bull run is not a life sentence either.

And it is fully invested on every trade, which is doing more than it looks. A small account running the identical rules pays the same three cents a share on far fewer shares, so the cost line stops being a quarter of the gross and starts being most of it.

The equities history I have runs out at the end of March 2026, so thats where it stops.
